validity.recommendation: Keep P0174 and P0146 as SEPARATE rows - do not merge; they are rival consortia, not one project
validity.researcher_notes: ADJUDICATION of the P0174-vs-P0146 duplicate hypothesis raised by the orchestrator: they are NOT the same project. They are the two genuinely competing 2000s-era Alaska Highway proposals, and the evidence is regulatory, not inferential. (1) SEPARATE FERC DOCKETS, described side by side in separate sections of the SAME document: FERC's ANGTA Eleventh Report to Congress (Feb 2011) has 'B. Denali's Proposal ... Denali plans to construct and operate a gas treatment plant (GTP) near Prudhoe Bay and a 48-inch-diameter pipeline to transport up to 4.5 Bcf/d from the Alaska North Slope to the Alberta Hub ... Docket No. PF08-26-000' and, immediately following, 'C. TC Alaska's Proposal ... Docket No. PF09-11-000'. A regulator does not open two pre-filing dockets for one project. (2) SEPARATE SPONSORS: Denali = BP plc + ConocoPhillips (50/50 JV incorporated as Denali - The Alaska Gas Pipeline LLC, announced 2008-04-08); the Alaska Pipeline Project = TransCanada/TC Energy + ExxonMobil, built on TransCanada's 2008 AGIA licence from the State of Alaska. Denali's own filing acknowledges TransCanada's separate AGIA licence. (3) SEPARATE OPEN SEASONS, months apart: TC Alaska's closed 2010-07-30, Denali's closed 2010-10-04. (4) SEPARATE ENDINGS: Denali withdrew from pre-filing 2011-05-17 (ANGTA Twelfth Report); the APP continued and is recorded on P0146 as cancelled in 2014. (5) DIFFERENT PHYSICAL SCOPE: the ANGTA Twelfth Report describes the APP as 'a gas treatment plant (GTP) near Prudhoe Bay, about 58 miles of 32-inch-diameter pipeline from the processing plant at the Point Thomson Field to the GTP, and about 745 miles of 48-inch-diameter mainline pipeline from the GTP to the Alaska-Yukon border', versus Denali's 730-mile Alaska Mainline + 1,020-mile Canada Mainline to Blueberry Hill, AB. (6) The trade press treats them as rivals throughout: AP (2010-04-07) frames Denali's open season against the competing TransCanada/Exxon project, and NGI (2011-05-23) quotes TransCanada VP Tony Palmer on Denali - 'They're an independent project'. The shared 4,500 MMcf/d is not a duplication artefact but the consequence of both consortia sizing to the same contracted ANS gas volume, and each states it in its own documents. CAVEAT recorded rather than a clean confirmation: the two rows share a corridor (both follow the Alaska Highway from a Prudhoe Bay GTP) and a capacity, so a future reviewer will ask this question again - the answer belongs in ResearcherNotes on both rows. Separately, P0146's LengthKnown=1700.00 is labelled 'km' while every source for that project says 1,700 MILES; that is a defect on P0146, flagged in cross_row_leads, not a reason to merge.
